title: Torres jackfruit (Torres langka): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Torres jackfruit: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Torres jackfruit is a jackfruit variety from registered by IPB. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Torres is a registered jackfruit variety, also sold or known as Torres langka. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1991. IPB bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Torres jackfruit is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Torres langka, this is the same jackfruit. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [jackfruit variety finder](/crop-varieties/jackfruit), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit jackfruit fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A fruit of Torres weighs about 3500 grams. The flesh is golden yellow and firm and crispy.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** About 3.5 kg, golden yellow, firm, crisp, juicy bulbs, mild aroma.
Registered in 1991 with the Philippine Seed Board.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of the first jackfruit varieties registered, a smaller crisp type. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Torres jackfruit

Pick a selection by flesh: firm and crisp for fresh eating and processing, or soft and sweet. Grafted trees of a named selection bear true. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Torres langka the same as Torres?
items.a: Yes. Torres langka is another name for Torres. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Torres?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
